findings: Under the literal reading of OQ-56, Prop. 2 (l.306–313) holds at n = 0 only vacuously. The interior of a convex body of S(0) is a single point (subsingleton_corpsInterior_dim_zero), so the clauses about A ≠ B (the frontier points, the projective measure, the zero set) have no instance. Continuity holds because V is a point. These clauses have instances exactly when n ≥ 1: some convex body of S(n) has two distinct interior points iff 0 < n (exists_ne_corpsInterior_iff, with the explicit convex body stdCorpsConvexe n, the rays of |v_i| ≤ v_0). So « holds in every dimension » (OQ-56) means « holds for n ≥ 1, and trivially at n = 0 ».

At n = 0, l_V is not real-valued: l_V(A, A) = +∞ at the one point of V (hilbertLength_self_dim_zero), and l_V is finite everywhere iff n ≥ 1 (hilbertLength_ne_top_iff_pos). The « fonction continue sur V × V » of l.312 holds at n = 0 only for a function valued in [0, +∞]. If a real-valued function is meant, the literal reading fails at n = 0 as well, for the same cause as the « iff » reading: Déf. 1 gives coincident points no measure (OQ-45).

The planner's note on the target ([r], unchecked) that the segment clause (0) might need n ≥ 1 is false. isProjSegment_corpsInterior_iff carries no [NeZero n], and all five clauses of the strict n ≥ 1 assembly hold in every dimension except the « ← » half of the last one.
questions: OQ-56 (open). This file takes no side. It proves the literal form in every dimension (pseudo_longueur_corps_convexe_literal), with its printed-format Prop PseudoLongueurCorpsConvexeLiteral true for every n. The strict pseudo_longueur_corps_convexe remains the n ≥ 1 « iff » form. The two part ways exactly at n = 0 (pseudoLongueurCorpsConvexePrinted_iff_literal: Printed n ↔ Literal n ∧ 0 < n). Routing: under the literal answer, the mark goes on Benzecri.pseudo_longueur_corps_convexe_literal once this file graduates, with no Lean change, subject to the next question. Under the « iff » answer it goes on Benzecri.pseudo_longueur_corps_convexe if OQ-45 (a) rules n ≥ 1 implied, and otherwise the row stays partial.

« une fonction continue sur V × V » (l.312): real-valued, or valued in [0, +∞]? Reading taken: [0, +∞] (EReal), as the strict assembly and Mesure's pseudoLength already read it. Under the real-valued reading, the literal form also fails at n = 0 (hilbertLength_ne_top_iff_pos), and a mark in every dimension would need OQ-45 (b) (a point given measure 0). This bears on OQ-56's premise that the literal reading « holds in every dimension ».

Evidence on OQ-56 from the text, not a ruling: the paper derives 6° (l.249–251, « nulle si et seulement si M = N ») from Prop. 2 (l.303, « La propriété 6° résulte de la » [proposition 2]). Under the « iff » reading the derivation is immediate. Under the literal reading it also needs 1°'s l_V(M, M) = 0 (l.232), which l.297–298 calls trivial. So l.303 fits both readings and does not decide between them.

kb_proposals: A convex body of S(n) in every dimension is Benzecri.stdCorpsConvexe n (the rays of |v_i| ≤ v_0, isCorpsConvexeS_stdCorpsConvexe), and for n ≥ 1 it has two distinct interior points (exists_ne_corpsInterior_iff). Use it as a non-vacuity witness for statements about convex bodies.

The interior of a convex body of S(0) is one point (subsingleton_corpsInterior_dim_zero), and l_V ≡ +∞ there. A statement about A ≠ B in such an interior is vacuous at n = 0; a « real-valued » statement about l_V is false at n = 0 (hilbertLength_ne_top_iff_pos).
